title_en: Li Fuyun v. State — State Compensation Claim

full_text_en:
Li Fuyun v. State Compensation

[Ruling Summary]

According to the provisions of the Supreme People's Court's Reply on the Retroactive Effect of the State Compensation Law of the PRC and the Scope of Cases Accepted by the Compensation Committees of the People's Courts, where an act of a state organ or its personnel, when exercising functions and powers, infringes upon the lawful rights and interests of a citizen, legal person, or other organization, and such act occurred before December 31, 1994, but continued after January 1, 1995, the part that should be compensated before December 31, 1994, if there were no provisions at that time, shall be compensated by reference to the provisions of the State Compensation Law, based on the national average daily wage of the preceding year at the time the compensation decision is made.

Decision of the Compensation Committee of the Supreme People's Court

(2003) Fa Wei Pei Zi No. 3

Claimant for Compensation: Li Fuyun, male, born July 18, 1946, Han ethnicity, from Changyuan County, Henan Province, residing at: Dormitory of the 12th Railway Bureau Materials Office, 27 Xixian Street, Wanbailin District, Taiyuan City, Shanxi Province.

Obligor for Compensation: Shanxi High People's Court.

Legal Representative: Li Yuzhen, President.

On June 6, 1999, the claimant for compensation Li Fuyun, on the ground that he had been acquitted by retrial, requested the Shanxi High People's Court to compensate him with compensation payments for 3,118 days of infringement upon his personal freedom; to compensate for 500 days of lost wages, medical expenses of RMB 2,075.38, and transportation expenses of RMB 69; and to compensate for RMB 3,657 in cash that had been confiscated as illicit money. He also requested the return of 11 seized deposit certificates totaling RMB 23,150, and the interest as indicated on the certificates; the return of RMB 1,960 in seized cash and interest; the return of one seized video player and one tape recorder; and the return of one color TV, one gold ring, and ten cartons of cigarettes that had been seized but not transferred with the case file.

On April 24, 2003, the Shanxi High People's Court issued Decision (2000) Jin Fa Pei Zi No. 2, deciding to pay Li Fuyun compensation of RMB 45,642.40 for 2,027 days of restricted personal freedom; to pay compensation of RMB 2,850 for one video player and one tape recorder that had been seized and turned over to the state treasury; and to deny Li Fuyun's other requests. Li Fuyun disagreed with this decision and, within the statutory period, applied to the Compensation Committee of this Court for a compensation decision. He requested compensation of RMB 100,295.96 for 2,027 days of restricted personal freedom from April 14, 1990, to October 31, 1995, calculated based on the 2002 national average daily wage of RMB 49.48; requested compensation for his economic losses and mental distress during the wrongful conviction period in accordance with relevant provisions; and requested reimbursement for one or more trips to Beijing to apply for state compensation. The Compensation Committee of this Court tried this case in accordance with Article 21, Paragraph 2 of the State Compensation Law of the PRC.

Upon trial, it was found that: On April 14, 1990, Li Fuyun was criminally detained by the Taiyuan Public Security Bureau on suspicion of bribery, and was arrested on April 23, 1990, upon approval of the Taiyuan People's Procuratorate. On January 28, 1991, the Taiyuan People's Procuratorate issued Indictment (1990) Bing Jian Xing Qi Zi No. 100, charging Li Fuyun with the crimes of embezzlement and bribery, and initiated a public prosecution in the Taiyuan Intermediate People's Court. On April 8, 1991, the Taiyuan Intermediate People's Court issued Criminal Judgment (1991) Fa Xing Chu Zi No. 28, holding that the defendant Li Fuyun, by taking advantage of his position, embezzled RMB 9,000 and accepted bribes of over RMB 30,000, thus committing the crimes of embezzlement and bribery. The court sentenced the defendant Li Fuyun to five years' imprisonment for embezzlement and seven years' imprisonment for bribery, with a combined sentence of twelve years, to be executed as eleven years' imprisonment. At the same time, the court ordered the confiscation of the seized deposits and cash totaling RMB 28,327, one video player, and one tape recorder, to be turned over to the state treasury. Li Fuyun appealed against this judgment. On July 12, 1991, the Shanxi High People's Court issued Criminal Judgment (1991) Fa Xing Shang Zi No. 88, holding that Li Fuyun, by taking advantage of his position, embezzled RMB 9,000 and accepted bribes of over RMB 30,000, thus constituting the crimes of embezzlement and bribery. The court also found that while in custody, Li Fuyun had provided information regarding others' crimes, which was verified, and thus should be given a lighter punishment. The court accordingly set aside the part of the original judgment concerning the punishment of Li Fuyun, sentenced him to four years and six months' imprisonment for embezzlement and six years and six months' imprisonment for bribery, with a combined sentence of eleven years, to be executed as ten years' imprisonment, and affirmed the part of the original judgment concerning the confiscation of the related property and its turnover to the state treasury.

After the judgment became legally effective, Li Fuyun disagreed and filed multiple petitions. On July 21, 1998, the Shanxi High People's Court issued Criminal Order (1996) Jin Xing Jian Zi No. 63, ordering a retrial of the case by a newly constituted collegial panel.

On October 12, 1998, the Shanxi High People's Court issued Criminal Retrial Judgment (1996) Jin Xing Zai Zhong Zi No. 63, holding that during Li Fuyun's tenure as manager of the Labor Service Company of Taiyuan West Railway Station under the Taiyuan Railway Sub-Bureau, the company achieved operating profits of RMB 1,274,855. According to relevant documents, a business commission fund of RMB 61,193 could be withdrawn. Li Fuyun actually received RMB 31,430 in fees during business activities, which was RMB 29,763 less than the commission he was entitled to withdraw under the regulations. The over RMB 9,000 that Li Fuyun personally received was a personal reward stipulated in the documents. Li Fuyun's argument that the fees he withdrew were business expenses in accordance with the documents, used for business contacts, and did not constitute the crimes of embezzlement or bribery, should be accepted. The judgment set aside the Criminal Judgment (1991) Fa Xing Chu Zi No. 28 of the Taiyuan Intermediate People's Court and the Criminal Judgment (1991) Fa Xing Shang Zi No. 88 of the Shanxi High People's Court, and acquitted Li Fuyun.

It was also found that Li Fuyun was released on parole on October 31, 1995, and had actually been in custody for 2,027 days.

The Compensation Committee of this Court held that the claimant for compensation, Li Fuyun, having been acquitted by retrial, is entitled to state compensation in accordance with the law. The Decision (2000) Jin Fa Pei Zi No. 2 of the Shanxi High People's Court correctly found the facts of this case and correctly applied the provisions of the Reply on the Retroactive Effect of the State Compensation Law of the PRC and the Scope of Cases Accepted by the Compensation Committees of the People's Courts, and the compensation by reference to the State Compensation Law was also correct. However, the decision improperly applied the law by using the 1994 national average daily wage as the reference standard for compensation. According to Article 26 of the State Compensation Law and Article 6, Paragraph 1 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the People's Courts' Implementation of the State Compensation Law of the PRC, compensation for infringement of personal freedom shall be calculated at the national average daily wage of the preceding year at the time the compensation decision is made by the obligor for compensation, the reconsideration organ, or the compensation committee of the people's court. In accordance with the above provisions and the Reply on the Retroactive Effect of the State Compensation Law of the PRC and the Scope of Cases Accepted by the Compensation Committees of the People's Courts, where an act of a state organ or its personnel, when exercising functions and powers, infringes upon the lawful rights and interests of a citizen, legal person, or other organization, and such act occurred before December 31, 1994, but continued after January 1, 1995, the part that should be compensated before December 31, 1994, if there were no provisions at that time, shall be compensated by reference to the provisions of the State Compensation Law. According to the above provisions, this case should be compensated based on the national average daily wage of the preceding year at the time the compensation decision is made. The claimant's request to be compensated for 2,027 days of restricted personal freedom from April 14, 1990, to October 31, 1995, at the 2002 national average daily wage standard, should be supported. Li Fuyun's requests for compensation for other economic losses and mental distress during the wrongful conviction period, as well as reimbursement for one or more trips to Beijing to apply for state compensation, are not within the scope of compensation under the State Compensation Law and are not supported by this Court.

Pursuant to Article 15, Item (3) and Article 26 of the State Compensation Law of the PRC, Article 6, Paragraph 1 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the People's Courts' Implementation of the State Compensation Law of the PRC, and Article 1 of the Reply on the Retroactive Effect of the State Compensation Law of the PRC and the Scope of Cases Accepted by the Compensation Committees of the People's Courts, it is hereby decided as follows:

1. Item 1 of Decision (2000) Jin Fa Pei Zi No. 2 of the Shanxi High People's Court is set aside;

2. The Shanxi High People's Court shall pay the claimant for compensation, Li Fuyun, compensation of RMB 100,295.96 for 2,027 days of infringement upon his personal freedom;

3. Items 2 and 3 of Decision (2000) Jin Fa Pei Zi No. 2 of the Shanxi High People's Court are affirmed.

This decision is legally effective.

November 7, 2003
